topic.readerProblem: Someone who finds Evertune too expensive, demo-gated or too large for their team wants a shortlist of alternatives with real entry prices and an honest view of when Evertune is still the better pick.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether AI engines name a brand; this page helps buyers choose between a one-off audit like AEOeye, cheap self-serve trackers and an enterprise platform, and teaches them to compare vendors by cost per answer and sampling rather than headline prompt counts.

assessment: The page derives the reasons to leave Evertune from its own pricing, Advertise and company pages (demo-only entry at $800 a month, a content-and-ads bundle, a mid-market-and-up target) instead of reviewer rumors, and drops the older page's unverified $3,000-a-month floor, US-panel limit and engine claims. It lists AEOeye, Otterly.AI, Peec AI, AthenaHQ and Profound with entry prices and limits read from each vendor's own pricing page on 3 October 2026, adds worked cost-per-answer arithmetic from the vendors' own figures (Peec Starter 4,500 answers for $95; AthenaHQ Starter 3,600 credits for $295), and ends with when Evertune is still the right choice. It states that it rests on public documentation and does not claim hands-on testing of any tool but AEOeye. It deliberately does not rank the tools, claim any vendor lacks a feature it does not list, or convert currencies.

sources.supports: Pro $800 / month (100,000 prompts across 11 AI models; daily, weekly or monthly tracking; global language and country tracking; 25 AI-optimized articles a month; 3 onboarding sessions; affiliate advertising partnerships; AI Retargeting; 'for mid-market brands'); Enterprise custom (dedicated AI Success Manager, customized onboarding, deep category analysis, unlimited content generation, AI website optimization, AI bot analytics, SSO); both plans use 'Request a demo'.

Ads Manager runs ChatGPT advertising from visibility insights; the retargeting section is offered as a beta ('Join the beta'); Evertune calls itself the first GEO platform to turn organic AI visibility into paid reach.
Evertune works with mid-market and enterprise brands.
Evertune's July 2026 running-shoes experiment: ±9 points overall and ±31 points at topic level when each of 100 prompts is asked once, versus ±1 and ±2 when asked 100 times.

Lite $29 / month (15 prompts, daily tracking, ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot; Claude, AI Mode and Gemini as add-ons); Standard $189 / month (100 prompts); free trial offered; annual billing 15% off.

Read in a rendered browser: Starter $95 / month (50 prompts, choose 3 models, unlimited users, daily, 1 project; 4,500 monthly AI answers = prompts x models x frequency), Pro $245 (150 prompts), Advanced $495 (350 prompts); Enterprise custom; 15% annual discount; crawlability audit across 40+ AI bots; free trial button.

Free plan with $25 credit (300 credits) across five engines; Starter $295 / month for 3,600 credits across 11 models; 1 credit = 1 AI response; API access and extra credits are paid add-ons; annual billing 17% off; Enterprise custom.

Brand plans are a free Trial (50 prompts run daily for 7 days on ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews, limited AI Marketer credits) and Enterprise (custom, up to 9 answer engines, SSO/SAML and SOC 2).
AI brand lists rarely repeat across runs; advice to ask at least 60-100 times and average.

checks: Writer (Sonnet): downloaded the pricing pages of Evertune, Otterly.AI, Profound and AthenaHQ with curl on 2026-10-03 and read the raw page text; Peec AI's prices are JavaScript-rendered, so I loaded peec.ai/pricing in a browser and read Starter $95, Pro $245, Advanced $495 and the 4,500 monthly answers from the rendered page.

Writer (Sonnet): confirmed on Evertune's own pricing, Advertise, get-started and company pages that the page shows Pro at $800 a month, no trial and no billing terms, and a mid-market-and-up target; I dropped the earlier page's $3,000-a-month floor, US-centric-panel concern, Otterly 14-day trial and $489 Premium, Peec 14-day trial and Profound ~$99 self-serve claims because the current pricing pages do not show them.

Writer (Sonnet): computed the cost-per-answer figures myself (95/4,500 = $0.021; 295/3,600 = $0.082; 800 x 12 = $9,600) and labelled them on the page as our arithmetic from vendor-stated numbers; I did not compute a per-answer price for Evertune because its page does not define what its 100,000 prompts count.

Writer (Sonnet): checked the AI-visibility-vendor rows of the AEOeye crawler access study (0 of 43 block an AI bot; llms.txt 27 of 41; homepage FAQPage 18 of 42) against the evidence pack before using them, with the study's denominators.
